title: The cause of self‐heating of npk compound fertilisers containing nitrates
abstract: AbstractAttack by nitrates on organic matter contained in granular fertilisers is a major cause of self‐heating of bulk storage heaps. Methods are described by which the organic matter in superphosphates can be destroyed or modified prior to the manufacture of granular compound fertilisers.Oxidation of the organic material by nitrates can be inhibited by substances capable of reacting with nitrous acid, notably urea. Production‐scale trials prove that small amounts of urea can adequately control this, and in addition, incorporation of urea reduces nitrous gas evolution from NPK fertilisers and enables these materials to be stored satisfactorily in multiwall paper sacks.Under certain conditions, inter‐ionic reaction between potassium chloride and an ammonium nitrate/potassium nitrate solid solution can also cause significant temperature rises. Such self‐heating can be limited by reducing the residual water content of the granular fertiliser, or by other variations in manufacturing procedure.
